A1 Reading mini-drill
Passage
A city library introduced a “quiet hour” every weekday morning. During that hour, phone calls are
not allowed and group rooms remain closed. The policy was first tested for one month. Surveys later
showed that most students found it easier to concentrate, although some asked the library to keep
one room available for discussion. The library has decided to continue the policy while opening a
separate discussion room on another floor.
1. Why was the quiet hour introduced? A. To reduce staff work. B. To support concentration. C. To close
group rooms permanently. D. To attract more visitors.
2. What can be inferred about the library? A. It ignored student feedback. B. It ended the policy. C. It
adjusted the policy after feedback. D. It banned all discussion.
3. What does “although” signal? A. Cause B. Contrast C. Example D. Time
4. Which is NOT true? A. Calls are restricted during quiet hour. B. The trial lasted a month. C. Every
student supported the original policy. D. A separate room will allow discussion.
5. Best title? A. A Library Balances Quiet Study and Discussion B. Why Phones Are Harmful C. The History
of City Libraries D. Students Need Longer Holidays
Answers: 1-B, 2-C, 3-B, 4-C, 5-A.
A2 Grammar filling mini-drill
A community garden, ___(start) by local residents three years ago, now provides fresh vegetables for
dozens of families. It ___(become) a meeting place as well. Every Saturday, volunteers work
together, and younger children learn ___ to care for plants. The garden is much ___(green) than the
empty lot that was there before, and many residents say it has made ___ neighborhood feel more
connected.
Answers: started; has become; how; greener; the.
A3 Practical writing mini-task
Your school English club will hold a short film night. Write an email to an exchange student: introduce the
event, give time/place, and invite the student to join.

rows:
Checklist before writing: event + time/place + what is interesting + clear invitation/reply request.
Do not start by searching for an advanced phrase.

A4 Continuation planning mini-task
Story situation: A student misses the last bus after a competition and has little phone battery left. Given
openings: (1) Just then, a familiar voice called my name. (2) When we finally reached my street, the
lights in my house were still on.
1. Who can reasonably be the familiar person based on earlier story context?
2. What must happen in paragraph 1 so paragraph 2 can begin “When we finally reached my street”?
3. What is the main emotional line?
4. What problem should paragraph 2 resolve?
